content: If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the potential benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. This medication may increase your blood pressure. In rare cases, it has been associated with severe, and occasionally fatal, sudden worsening of breathing problems or asthma, a condition known as paradoxical bronchospasm. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. If you are in Canada, do the same. Precautions: Before using epinephrine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to similar bronchodilators (such as albuterol, levalbuterol, or salmeterol), to sympathomimetic drugs (such as pseudoephedrine), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this dizziness. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is unknown whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid using MAO inhibitors (such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, or tranylcypromine) or tricyclic antidepressants (such as amitriptyline or nortriptyline) within two weeks before, during, or after treatment with this medication. Caffeine can increase the side effects of this medication. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and is experiencing serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Monitoring: While using this medication, your doctor may perform laboratory or medical tests (such as blood pressure, heart rate, EKG, or blood potassium levels) to monitor your progress and check for side effects. Be sure to keep all medical and laboratory appointments. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. Do not puncture the canister or expose it to high heat or open flames. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your condition may cause complications in a medical emergency. Ensure that medical personnel are aware of your condition. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Epinephrine is used to treat wheezing and shortness of breath commonly associated with asthma. Controlling these symptoms can reduce time lost from work or school. Epinephrine belongs to a class of drugs known as bronchodilators. It works by relaxing the muscles around the airways, allowing them to open up so you can breathe more easily. How to Use: Read the Patient Information Leaflet for instructions on the proper use of this medication and the correct cleaning of the mouthpiece. Shake the canister well before each inhalation. Follow all directions on the product package. If you have any questions, ask your doctor or pharmacist. Use this medication exactly as directed in the product package. Inhale by mouth as needed. Remove the cap from the mouthpiece. Place the mouthpiece near your mouth and exhale. Insert the mouthpiece fully into your mouth and press the inhaler as you breathe in deeply. Hold your breath for as long as comfortable to allow the drug to be absorbed. If more than one inhalation is needed, wait at least one full minute between inhalations. Do not use again for at least four hours. Rinse your mouth after using this medication to help prevent dryness and throat irritation. Clean the mouthpiece after each day of use as directed. Keep track of the number of inhalations used from each canister. Discard the canister after you have used the number of inhalations marked on the product package. Side Effects: Common side effects may include headache, nausea, vomiting, nervousness, dizziness, shaking (tremor), trouble sleeping, stomach upset, sweating, dry mouth, bad taste, cough, or sore throat. If your doctor has directed you to use this medication, remember that they have judged the benefit to you to be greater than the risk of side effects. This medication may raise your blood pressure. Rarely, it has caused severe (and rarely fatal) sudden worsening of breathing problems or asthma (paradoxical bronchospasm). Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the U.S., call your doctor for medical advice about side effects. If you are in Canada, do the same.
